text: Full-Mouth Reconstruction in McLean & Alexandria, VA

When teeth are worn, broken, failing or missing across the mouth, a prosthodontist rebuilds them together, with implants, crowns, bridges and veneers chosen to fit one design and one bite. Board-certified prosthodontist Dr. Esam Nahlah plans it and restores it.

Not a list of treatments. One mouth, rebuilt as a system.
Full-mouth reconstruction, which prosthodontists also call full-mouth rehabilitation, restores most or all of the teeth in both jaws. Rather than fixing one tooth at a time, the specialist plans
: how the teeth look, how the upper and lower meet, and what each tooth needs to get there.
When one tooth at a time stops working.

Worn and broken teeth, several missing teeth, gum disease and a bite that no longer meets evenly tend to arrive together, and they are often one problem: once a tooth is lost, the bone under it deteriorates and the damage spreads to its neighbors.
Because a prosthodontist reads the whole mouth as one system, the question at your first visit is not
which tooth do I fix first
what does the finished mouth need
. A second opinion on a plan you already have costs nothing.
What a reconstruction can be built from.
Most plans combine several of these; the design decides which tooth gets which.
Custom caps over natural teeth that are too worn, cracked or stained for anything thinner.
Linked crowns that fill a gap. Carried on implants, a zirconia bridge leaves the healthy teeth beside it untouched.
Hand-designed porcelain over less than a millimeter of enamel, for front teeth that are chipped, spaced or stained.
Where teeth are missing or beyond saving, implants carry the new teeth, from a single crown to a fixed zirconia arch.
How a reconstruction is planned and built.
Time with Dr. Nahlah, your goals, a free digital preview of how the result will look, and the options with their prices.
A complete examination and a cone-beam scan of both jaws, to find what needs treating before anything else: gum disease, failing teeth, missing bone.
Shape, shade, proportion and bite settled for the whole mouth, and approved by you before any tooth is prepared.
Treatment in the sequence the plan sets, which can mean extractions and grafting before implants and crowns, with the lab in the building adjusting shade and fit.

faq: Rebuilding most or all of the teeth in both jaws to one plan, with crowns, bridges, veneers and implants as the case needs. Prosthodontists call it full-mouth rehabilitation, and it is the core of the specialty.
How is it different from a smile makeover?
A smile makeover works mostly on the teeth that show. A full-mouth reconstruction rebuilds the whole mouth, back teeth and bite included, often with implants where teeth are missing.

Usually people with several problems at once: worn or broken teeth, several missing teeth, gum disease or a bite that no longer meets evenly. The examination and scan decide whether the whole mouth needs rebuilding or only part of it.
It is done in stages, in the order the design requires. Where implants are part of it, allow anywhere from a few months to over a year, longer if bone has to be grafted first.
Can I see the result before treatment starts?
Yes. A digital preview of the finished smile is built from photos and scans of your mouth, free, and you approve the design before any tooth is prepared.
The price is set with the plan at the consultation. Most PPO dental plans are accepted, claims are filed for you, and financing reaches $60,000 over terms of up to 96 months.
